title: Cubic Hecke Timer Threads
objective: Make Hecke class-unit benchmark timings root-contiguous and bind Julia t1/t4 resource identity

handoff.summary: Corrected the Hecke comparator so every retained warm timing is one direct contiguous root interval. Persistent cells first complete and discard an independently root-timed calibration of at least 1.2 seconds, then time a fresh retained batch; field, computation, and proof-upgrade timers remain nested attribution and cannot be summed into the root. Added exact --julia-threads 1|4 control across execution argv, generated-runtime assertion, authenticated runtime probe, tool execution identity, v4 receipt configuration/jobs, and the semantic comparison identity. Focused counterfeits reject phase-sum roots, mismatched config/job resources, stale t1 semantics in t4 evidence, and indistinguishable t1/t4 tools. The full build, focused 18-test suite, Node syntax check, and Julia Meta.parseall check pass. No opt or holdout workload was run.
risks: The current integration base has unrelated validation drift: architecture:check reports a stale native-export inventory; test:portable reports the new rectangular-binary64 lowering missing from an expected registry; test:baselib:strict reports two undefined optimizer runtime names in src/baselib/containers.py. This lane claims none of those files.

The retained kernel-warm batch prepares independent fields and maximal orders before its root interval, so very fast cases may retain many prepared objects until the batch completes; the 100000-iteration safety limit remains fail-closed.
Only generated-source structure and Julia parsing were exercised locally; the requested opt smoke/tune measurements remain intentionally unscheduled here.
next_steps: Integrate this stop-ship correction before producing any new Hecke performance receipt.
After candidate freeze, run t1 as the primary Hecke smoke/tune profile and label t4 separately as a resource race; do not combine their receipt or semantic identities.
Keep the holdout tier sealed until the parent campaign explicitly opens it.
